answer: Shared Operator Liability Pool. Each agent wallet maps to a verified operator entity; every identity an operator controls draws from one pooled collateral reserve. A fraud proven against any single wallet triggers a proportional draw on the whole pool, so a dune of fake identities collapses one operator's backing at once. The catch: an attacker must over-collateralize every duplicate on the same knoll of capital, and one detection sends a ripple through all of them. Per-identity cost is the full pool fraction, not a cheap standalone bond.
